learning: If slalom max_error falls to 0.06 m or below and slalom progress rises above 0.30 with oval and s-bend completion holding, the mismatch bias was the slalom limit and ki can go higher. If s-bend completion drops below 18/20 or oscillation rises sharply, the integral is overshooting, so return ki to 0.2 and test wheel_track of about 0.10 m next.
notes: Geometry is the iteration-6 Builder geometry, unchanged. The controller is the iteration-6 controller with ki raised from 0.2 to 0.4, so the integral term is the only controller variable. Full measurement set requested.
rationale: Iteration 6 is the best race so far at 670.5. Oval (20/20) and s-bend (20/20) both complete, and the slalom still fails 0/20 with progress 0.30, max_error 0.063 m (just above the 0.06 m limit) and 1.05 line-loss events per run. The Builder held geometry at y = 0.07 m, x = ±0.024 m, 0.6 kg, which matches the iteration-6 geometry and the Integrator's plan. Line losses are far below the 2-per-run widening trigger, and iteration 5 showed that extra look-ahead gives no slalom gain, so geometry is not the limit. The only controller term that has moved slalom progress is the integral term: iteration 4 added ki = 0.2 and slalom progress rose from 0.198 to 0.278, while the motor mismatch in the contract is a steady bias that a small ki only partly removes. This race therefore raises ki from 0.2 to 0.4 and keeps kp 2.4, kd 0.8, base_speed 1.3 and last_direction line loss, so ki is the only controller change. Integral windup is limited to ±2, and oval and s-bend oscillation (0.18 and 0.30) leave some margin. I expect slalom max_error to move toward 0.06 m and progress to rise, with oval and s-bend completion holding. This is a hypothesis, not a measured result. The main risk is overshoot after bends from the larger integral, which would show as lower s-bend completion or higher oscillation.
